job.title: Manager, Mobile Software Engineering
job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide.

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Intro to Position

Do you want to play a major role in the future of public media? Do you have a passion for mobile technology, open-source software, and serving the public?

As our Mobile Software Engineering Manager on the Audience Technology team, you will lead a highly collaborative team of mobile software engineers building, testing, and delivering award-winning features for NPR's flagship mobile applications. You will partner closely with our Product, Design, Data, and Editorial teams to identify priorities, architect new features, and continuously improve existing applications. In this role, you will act as a primary champion of team health, career progression, and technical excellence.

Responsibilities

  • People Leadership & Coaching: Manage, mentor, and coach a team of Mobile Software Engineers, actively investing in their career growth, professional development, and psychological safety.
  • Talent Acquisition & Onboarding: Lead recruitment and hiring efforts for software engineering vacancies on your team, and manage the structured onboarding and training of new engineering staff.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with product managers, UX designers, data analysts, and editorial partners across all stages of the product development lifecycle.
  • Agile Delivery Management: Lead the technical planning, scoping, and execution of future software projects, facilitating Agile ceremonies (stand-ups, backlog refinements, sprint planning, and retrospectives) as needed.
  • Technical Quality & Code Review: Conduct thorough software design and code reviews, providing constructive and substantive feedback to maintain code health, architectural integrity, and security standards.
  • Continuous Process Improvement: Analyze, propose, and implement engineering workflow improvements to enhance the speed, safety, and quality of software delivery.
  • Developer Experience Automation: Identify common engineering blockers and pain points, writing helper tools or automation scripts to optimize team developer experience (DX).
  • Incident & Production Support: Oversee and coordinate the team's response to critical mobile production bugs or infrastructure incidents.
  • Vendor & Contributor Management: Coordinate workflows, code standards, and deliverables for external contributors and specialized development vendors.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 2+ years of experience directly managing, mentoring, or leading mobile software engineers within an agile organization.
  • Prior experience as an individual contributor in engineering, testing, and shipping robust code for at least one large-scale mobile application.
  • Hands-on proficiency in modern mobile platform languages, specifically Swift/Objective-C (iOS) or Kotlin/Java (Android).
  • Strong working knowledge of native mobile release infrastructures (such as Apple App Store Connect/provisioning profiles or Google Play Console/staged rollouts).
  • Hands-on experience working with modern version control systems (primarily Git).
  • Demonstrated experience collaborating within cross-functional Agile/Scrum product teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Professional experience managing both internal employees and external agency vendors/contractors.
  • Experience with native mobile media streaming frameworks (such as AVKit/AVFoundation for iOS, or Media3/ExoPlayer for Android).
  • Familiarity with modern responsive design architectures (SwiftUI/Combine or Jetpack Compose/Coroutines), design patterns (MVVM), and automotive platforms (CarPlay/Android Auto).

Required Skills/Competencies

  • Technical Design & Communication: Ability to translate complex technical concepts, system architectures, and engineering trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Inclusive Leadership: Demonstrated competency in fostering an equitable, supportive, and inclusive team culture.
  • Systemic Problem Solving: Strong analytical skill set with an "automation-first" mindset for resolving manual bottlenecks and production issues.
  • User-Centric Empathy: A strong focus on quality and empathy for end-users, ensuring highly performant, accessible mobile application experiences.
  • Agile Operations: Deep fluency in Agile methodologies and software project delivery management.

Education Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or equivalent practical work experience.

Work Location & Requirements

  • NPR Remote-Permitted: This is a remote-permitted role. This role is based out of our Washington, D.C. office, but the employee may choose to work on a remote basis from a location that NPR approves. You will have the option of working (a) remotely from a location of your choosing within the United States that is supported by NPR; (b) on-site at an NPR facility, based on the availability of desks and approval from NPR; or (c) a combination of both. Regardless of where you choose to work from, you may be expected to travel to other locations from time to time to perform the duties of your position.

Job Type

  • This is a full-time, exempt position.

Compensation

Salary Range: The U.S.-based anticipated salary range for this opportunity is $165,000 - $175,000 plus benefits. The range displayed reflects the minimum and maximum salaries NPR expects to provide for new hires for the position across all US locations.

NPR Benefits: NPR provides comprehensive benefits for employees and dependents. Regular, full-time employees scheduled to work 30 hours or more per week are eligible to enroll in NPR’s benefits options. Benefits include access to health and wellness, paid time off, and financial well-being. Plan options include medical, dental, vision, life/ accidental death and dismemberment, long-term disability, short-term disability, and voluntary retirement savings to all eligible NPR employees.

Does this sound like you? If so, we want to hear from you.

job.title: Manager, eCommerce Marketing
job.description: We are UMG, the Universal Music Group. We are the world’s leading music company. In everything we do, we are committed to artistry, innovation and entrepreneurship. We own and operate a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content in more than 60 countries. We identify and develop recording artists and songwriters, and we produce, distribute and promote the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful music to delight and entertain fans around the world. Famehouse, a division of UMG, is the preeminent leader in D2C solutions in music, defining & delivering the industry’s best-in-class service to connect artists with their fans. Established & headquartered in Philly, Famehouse powers D2C for UMG’s labels, artists, and Bravado, along with a select roster of 3rd party clients. Our success & culture is fueled by collaboration—both within FH and with our partners. We are passionate about the impact of D2C & merchandise for artists, providing a full-service solution to grow an artist’s owned business including strategy, creative, storefront merchandising, fulfillment, customer service, technology, and more. How we LEAD: Merchandise and commerce are part of the fabric of music culture. For artists, it’s a way to develop and further articulate their brand. For fans, it’s another pathway to connecting with an artist and the culture they represent. The Manager, Site Marketing turns traffic, campaign demand, product priorities, and artist moments into high-impact storefront strategies that drive conversion, sell-through, fan engagement, and revenue growth. This role owns the non-creative site strategy across merchandising, product placement, promotional planning, campaign destinations, homepage, and collection strategy, PDP optimization, key shopping moments, and alignment with CRM, paid media, and other acquisition channels. Core responsibilities of this role include: Lead on-site marketing programming across the sites, including promotions, to achieve store revenue and conversion goals. Optimize fan journeys from traffic source to product discovery, storytelling, offer, and purchase. Align cross-channel execution with paid media, email, CRM, social, label, and artist teams. Merchandise and prioritize products, collections, campaigns, and offers on the storefront to drive engagement, conversion, and revenue. Identify opportunities to improve site performance through testing, merchandising adjustments, landing page optimization, offer strategy, and improved shopping paths. Translate artist priorities, label needs, inventory considerations, product performance, and commercial goals into an actionable site plan. This role requires a strategic, commercially minded, highly collaborative manager who can balance long-term planning with fast-moving priorities. The ideal candidate understands how fans shop, how campaigns translate across ecommerce storefronts, and how product performance should inform merchandising, promotional, and customer journey decisions. They should be comfortable leading workstreams, making clear recommendations, building alignment across cross-functional partners, and bringing structure, judgment, and momentum to a high-volume environment. How you'll CREATE: Site Marketing Strategy & Commercial Planning Own site marketing strategy for a portfolio of artist stores, ensuring storefront activity aligns to commercial priorities, artist moments, fan demand, and revenue goals. Build and manage site marketing calendars that coordinate releases, product drops, promotions, tour moments, seasonal opportunities, CRM pushes, paid media campaigns, and evergreen selling periods. Prioritize the highest-value opportunities across stores and campaigns, balancing business impact, artist priorities, product performance, traffic drivers, and operational feasibility. Translate campaign demand, product priorities, and artist moments into clear storefront plans that define what should show up, where it should appear, when it should launch, and how it should support conversion. Lead planning conversations with cross-functional partners to ensure site strategy is proactive, commercially grounded, and clearly connected to broader marketing and revenue goals. On-Site Campaigns, Promotions & Merchandising Lead planning and execution of on-site marketing campaigns that support new releases, product launches, catalog moments, artist exclusives, preorders, restocks, tour activity, limited-edition drops, and seasonal moments. Own merchandising recommendations across homepages, collections, product pages, campaign destinations, navigation paths, cart moments, and other key storefront placements. Determine how products, collections, campaigns, and offers are surfaced, sequenced, and prioritized to improve product discovery, fan engagement, conversion, average order value, and sell-through. Develop promotional strategies across sitewide and artist-specific moments, including offer placement, messaging, landing page strategy, timing, and coordination with CRM, paid media, and other marketing channels. Use proven ecommerce levers such as discounts, bundles, free shipping, gift-with-purchase, exclusives, presale access, urgency messaging, and limited-time moments to support demand capture and conversion. Ensure storefront plans reflect artist brand, campaign strategy, customer needs, and commercial opportunity while making it easy for fans to discover and purchase priority products. job.description: Part-Time Producer – ESPN Milwaukee & WTMJ (Milwaukee, WI) Good Karma Sports is looking for a Part-Time Producer to support programming across ESPN Milwaukee and WTMJ. This teammate will provide production support across both brands based on programming and coverage needs, including live and recorded shows, play-by-play broadcasts, and other audio and content production. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys working in a live broadcast environment, can think on their feet, and is interested in building experience across sports, news/talk, audio, and broadcast production. The Part-Time Producer will collaborate with hosts, broadcasters, producers, and other teammates to help deliver high-quality programming and content across ESPN Milwaukee and WTMJ. Hours will vary based on programming and coverage needs and will primarily include evenings and weekends. Career responsibilities include but are not limited to: Operate the radio board for live, syndicated, and locally produced programming, maintaining appropriate audio levels and smoothly transitioning between sources. Provide production support for ESPN Milwaukee and WTMJ programming as assigned. Support live play-by-play broadcasts and special programming, including coordinating with hosts, broadcasters, producers, and technical teammates. Work with hosts and broadcasters on show preparation, content planning, production elements, and live show execution. Complete broadcast logs and help ensure programming, commercials, sponsorships, contesting, and other scheduled elements air accurately. Create and implement production elements, including bumps, liners, promos, audio drops and other audio content. Edit and publish show podcasts, show audio, interviews, and other content for station and digital platforms. Assist with audio, video, and other production needs supporting programming, broadcasts, station initiatives, and events as needed. Set up and operate cameras and other production equipment for live broadcasts, events, and special programming as needed. Collaborate with producers, marketing teammates, engineering teammates, and others to support programming and station needs across ESPN Milwaukee and WTMJ. Help identify and communicate technical issues and support the accurate execution of programming in accordance with applicable FCC requirements. Stay informed about Wisconsin sports, local news, and other topics relevant to ESPN Milwaukee and WTMJ programming. Use approved AI tools to support research, content development, audio and video production, editing, and production efficiency while reviewing all AI-assisted work for accuracy, quality, and alignment with brand standards. Complete other assigned tasks as needed. Be a Good Karma Sports ambassador and adhere to the core values: Listen, Be Honest, Work Hard, Over Deliver, Follow Through, and Teamwork. Preferred knowledge, skills and qualifications Interest in sports, news/talk, radio, podcasting, or live content production. Previous radio board operation, broadcast production, or live sports production experience preferred. Experience with Adobe Audition or similar audio-editing software preferred. Basic experience setting up or operating cameras and video production equipment for live events preferred. Strong attention to detail and the ability to remain organized during live, deadline-driven broadcasts. Effective written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with hosts, broadcasters, producers, engineers, and other teammates. Willingness to learn new broadcast systems, production tools, and processes. Flexible availability, including evenings and weekends, based on programming and coverage needs. Hours/Salary/Benefits Good Karma part-time teammates are paid hourly, with opportunities for increased pay as they develop additional skills and responsibilities. Weekly hours will vary based on programming, play-by-play, and coverage needs across ESPN Milwaukee and WTMJ. This position will primarily require evening and weekend availability. Opportunity for Growth Teammates have the opportunity to continuously learn and grow within Good Karma and are responsible for representing Good Karma Sports, our story, and our core values inside and outside the workplace. Teammates are encouraged to take a proactive role in building relationships and seeking opportunities throughout the company. About Good Karma Sports Good Karma Sports is a sports media and marketing company that helps brands build meaningful connections with fans in and around the game. Combining national reach, regional expertise and deep local relationships, the company develops and executes multi-platform strategies across audio, podcasts, video, digital, social, talent, live experiences and premium sports partnerships. job.description: OVERVIEW OF THE COMPANY Fox News Media FOX News Media operates the FOX News Channel (FNC), FOX Business Network (FBN), FOX News Digital, FOX News Audio, FOX News Books, the direct-to-consumer digital streaming services FOX Nation and FOX News International and the newly announced platform FOX Weather. Currently the number one network in all of cable, FNC has also been the most watched television news channel for 20 consecutive years, while FBN currently ranks among the top business channels on cable. Owned by FOX Corporation, FOX News Media reaches 200 million people each month. JOB DESCRIPTION We are looking for a talented Line Producer to join the Fox & Friends team. As a Line Producer on Fox & Friends, your main daily responsibility will be translating the editorial vision for the show into an organized rundown and overseeing its live production on air. This includes building the rundown, making timing decisions, copy-editing segments, producing opens and teases, and communicating directly with anchors and executives. The Line Producer for Fox & Friends must be assertive, detail-oriented, and a natural self-starter who is not afraid to take control and lead a team. You should also have outstanding judgment, organizational skills, and creativity in teases and scripts. Most of all, you must be an effective communicator who can serve as the main point of contact for producers, directors, and talent/crew in the field. job.title: Manager, Flag Football
job.description:
The NFL is seeking a Manager, Flag Football to play a key role in driving the growth of youth flag football. This individual will be responsible for growing global youth participation, with a focus on the U.S., and is a critical member of the Flag integrated team, collaborating across the League, 32 NFL Clubs, and the broader flag football ecosystem to accelerate the growth of flag football.

This is a key leadership role that, in partnership with internal and external stakeholders, will play a formative role in the development of the youth flag football ecosystem during a period of exciting growth. This role requires strategic thinking, operational prowess, and strong partnership management skills. The Manager will serve as the point of contact for key strategic partnerships and will work closely with leaders across the League (including in Football Operations, International, Marketing, Comms, Events, Club Business Development, and Social Responsibility) to operationalize these partnerships and other key initiatives in the flag space. This position reports to the VP, Flag Football and offers significant exposure to senior NFL executives and an opportunity to shape the future of flag football at a national and global level.

Responsibilities

  • Develop & Execute Growth Strategy – Lead initiatives to expand youth flag football participation, driving engagement among key audiences, including players, parents, coaches, officials, and administrators.
  • Manage Strategic Partnerships – Serve as the primary liaison for key partners on flag football, including RCX Sports, GENYOUth, other youth organizations, and federations, ensuring operational alignment and maximizing impact.
  • Lead & Execute Flag Football Events – Serve as Flag lead for all youth- focused flag activations, including NFL FLAG Championships. Lead strategy and drive collaboration across internal & external stakeholders, ensuring seamless execution and maximal impact.
  • Awareness & Engagement – Oversee all phases of the participation funnel, from increasing awareness to enhancing player development through innovative programs and resources.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration – Work closely with internal teams such as Marketing, Events, Sponsorship, and Broadcasting to integrate flag football initiatives into broader NFL priorities.
  • Lead Meetings & Stakeholder Engagement – Organize and lead meetings with League, Club, and external partners, operating as a strategic project manager driving agendas and actionable outcomes.
  • Support International Growth – Partner with the International Flag team to share best practices and assist with global event execution where needed.
  • Strategic Planning & Execution – Support the VP, Flag Football in continuing to build out and evolve long-term strategy and for youth flag football within the broader framework of the Global Flag Football team

Required Qualifications

  • B.A/B.S. required
  • Minimum 5+ years of professional experience, with a focus in partnership management, flag/youth football, sports events/operations, or consulting
  • Proven ability to lead and influence complex cross-functional teams and manage external partnerships. Experience working with marketing, media, and event teams is a plus
  • Exceptional project management skills with strong attention to detail
  • Proficiency in PowerPoint and presentation development
  • Strong oral and written communication skills, with the ability to navigate high-level discussions with discretion and sound judgment
  • Deep understanding of the NFL and football ecosystem

Key Attributes & Skills

  • Ability to work collaboratively across departments and with external partners
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects in high-pressure environments
  • Experience with data analysis, reporting tools/dashboards, and consumer insights is a plus
  • Experience operating youth sports events is a plus
  • Experience working internationally is a plus

Physical Demands

  • Ability to attend and work key Flag events and meetings

Travel

  • Travel 20%

Terms / Expected Hours of Work

  • NFL employees are required to work 40 hours per week in the office. This role may often require hours on nights and/or weekends as well.

The NFL expects to hire for this position near the middle of the range. $85,000—$110,000 USD

To learn more about our comprehensive benefits offerings, please visit: NFL BENEFITS

At the NFL, in-person work at our offices is a top priority because it allows us to collaborate more effectively, build stronger connections, and maintain the culture that drives our success. This role requires onsite presence at an NFL office or stadium location, and remote and/or hybrid working options are not offered.

We are looking for a self-motivated, creative storyteller who can capture the essence of what’s happening in the field and deliver it seamlessly across broadcast, digital, and social platforms. The ideal candidate understands how audiences consume content differently on television, mobile, and social media—and can adapt storytelling styles seamlessly. This role would require field shooting, editing, and executing live shots, while also producing content optimized for linear TV, station websites/apps, and social platforms such as Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, and YouTube. The winning candidate is tech-savvy, forward-thinking, and fluent in modern newsgathering tools and formats. You must be able to shoot with Sony XDCAM or similar ENG cameras, as well as mobile-first tools like iPhone, gimbals and emerging digital formats, with editing in Adobe Premiere or comparable platforms. Familiarity with ENG, SNG, and cellular “backpacks” (TVU, LiveU, etc.) for live transmission and file transfer is essential. Strong editing skills, excellent time management, clear communication, and a sharp editorial eye are critical. A commitment to high journalistic standards and visual excellence is a must. If you’re quick-thinking, adaptable, and thrive in a fast-paced, multi-platform newsroom, we want to hear from you. This position reports to the Chief Photographer. Responsibilities Shoot and edit VOs, VO-SOTs, and packages for broadcast, digital, and streaming platforms Create and adapt content for multi-platform distribution, including TV, web, app, and social media Serve as show editor, cutting and attaching video content into a newscast rundown (ENPS proficiency is a bonus) Produce vertical and mobile-first video optimized for platforms like Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts Collaborate with the Assignment Desk, reporters, and producers to cover stories and meet deadlines Work with producers to bring editorial vision to life through strong visuals, sequencing, and natural sound Identify opportunities for real-time social content and behind-the-scenes storytelling in the field Ensure all content meets journalistic, ethical, and brand standards across platforms Requirements Experience with non-linear editing systems (Adobe Premiere preferred) Understanding of multi-platform storytelling, including broadcast and social/digital video formats Previous newsroom experience preferred; military experience strongly considered Ability to carry up to 50 pounds of equipment Comfortable working in all weather conditions Valid driver’s license with a strong driving record; ability to operate large vehicles Proficiency with mobile journalism tools and emerging video technologies Strong organizational, time-management, and problem-solving skills Ability to work under pressure and make quick editorial decisions Strong interpersonal and communication skills A proactive, self-starter mindset with a “go-getter” attitude Equivalent military training (DINFOS) and related experience highly valued In-person attendance is required Values in Action At Hearst Television we tell stories every day. You can explain why tomorrow’s forecast matters, be a trusted voice when severe weather threatens, confidently report from the middle of a developing weather story, and bring energy and curiosity to a community event. Our ideal candidate will be one who thinks outside the box – can deliver a polished in-studio forecast and then turn right around and produce an engaging, memorable vertical video about a timely weather topic. Innovation is critical: whether it’s in the middle of a snowstorm or a community fair, you’re always looking for new and creative ways to tell the best story. We’re looking for a storyteller at heart: with the ability to write and craft a weather-related report fit for any screen. job.title: Chief Engineer
job.description: Sinclair's content technology is central to operational excellence and to connecting audiences with trusted news across broadcast, cable, streaming, and digital platforms. TNND is seeking an experienced, technology-focused Chief Engineer to lead engineering for its national news production operation. This role owns the reliability, performance, scalability, and lifecycle of TNND's live-production and media systems. The Chief Engineer leads the engineering team and turns operational needs into dependable workflows in partnership with editorial, production, operations, and Corporate technology teams. Networking, enterprise monitoring, cybersecurity, and shared-infrastructure decisions are Corporate-led; the Chief Engineer supplies broadcast requirements, supports implementation, and keeps TNND systems aligned with those standards. The successful candidate combines hands-on engineering depth with calm incident leadership, disciplined planning, and a service-oriented approach to daily live news. Key Responsibilities Engineering Leadership and Operational Ownership • Own the end-to-end technical health and operational readiness of TNND's production environment, with direct accountability for reliable daily live output across an extended and variable schedule. • Lead, develop, schedule, and set priorities for engineering staff and technical support coverage; establish clear escalation paths and ensure appropriate on-call response for critical operations. • Serve as TNND's senior engineering subject-matter expert and incident leader, coordinating rapid restoration, clear stakeholder communication, and follow-through during high-pressure production events. • Partner with editorial, production, operations, Corporate IT, digital, cybersecurity, facilities, and distribution teams to align technical systems with newsroom priorities; serve as TNND's broadcast liaison for Corporate-led networking, monitoring, security, and shared infrastructure. • Translate business and production requirements into documented architectures, standards, operating procedures, project plans, lifecycle roadmaps, and budget recommendations. Live Production and Control-Room Systems • Engineer, maintain, and support the integrated control-room ecosystem, including cameras and robotics, production switchers, automated production control, real-time graphics, studio displays, audio consoles and processing, intercom/IFB, teleprompters, tally, routing, multiviewers, sync/reference, video servers, record/playback, encoders/decoders, and contribution/distribution interfaces. • Administer and optimize Ross OverDrive automated production control for live news, including show and template configuration, rundown execution, device control, graphics/audio/robotics coordination, NRCS/MOS integration, operator workflows, recalls/macros, and tested manual fallback procedures. • Support Ross XPression Tessera/Tessera One and related XPression workflows for pixel-accurate, synchronized content across studio displays and video walls, including region mapping, real-time graphics and data, external video inputs, signal timing, playout control, and recovery procedures. • Validate software, firmware, control, graphics, and workflow changes in a test or rehearsal process before air; maintain approved configuration baselines and rollback plans. • Work directly with directors, producers, operators, editors, and graphics teams to improve repeatability while preserving the flexibility required for breaking news and late rundown changes. Newsroom, Media, and Distribution Workflows • Maintain dependable integrations among the newsroom computer system (NRCS), MOS-connected tools, ingest, editing, media asset management, shared storage, archive, graphics, playout, and distribution systems. • Support live feeds, file-based media, remote contributors, streaming, and broadcast contribution/distribution workflows, including metadata, timing, caption/data paths, and SCTE signaling where applicable. • Partner with content and operations teams to strengthen editing, live-production, field-gathering, remote-production, and multi-platform publishing workflows without compromising on-air reliability. Broadcast Systems and Corporate Technology Integration • Serve as the broadcast liaison to Corporate-managed technology services: define operational requirements and support implementation and troubleshooting of LAN/WAN connectivity, VLANs, QoS, multicast, routing, DNS/DHCP, secure remote access, identity, and time synchronization under Corporate architecture and policy. • Support TNND's current baseband SDI and compressed-IP media workflows, maintaining practical knowledge of applicable contribution, distribution, audio-over-IP, and production protocols such as NDI, SRT/RIST, and AES67/Dante where deployed. • Administer broadcast-specific Windows, macOS, and Linux systems and applications, coordinating shared-infrastructure changes involving virtualization, storage, databases, cloud services where applicable, patching, backups, access control, endpoint protection, and security hardening with Corporate IT and cybersecurity. • Create and maintain accurate signal-flow drawings, network diagrams, rack elevations, system inventories, configuration records, credentials-handling procedures, and support documentation. Monitoring, Reliability, Redundancy, and Disaster Recovery • Maintain broadcast-facing monitoring and use Corporate-approved enterprise monitoring, telemetry, logging, alarming, and reporting tools so engineering and operations have appropriate visibility into system health, quality, and service status. • Design and maintain redundancy for critical workflows; define recovery priorities with stakeholders; document and regularly test failover, backup, restore, and disaster-recovery procedures. • Lead incident, problem, and change management for production technology, including root-cause analysis, corrective actions, maintenance windows, risk communication, and post-incident learning. • Manage preventive maintenance, lifecycle replacement, spares, warranties, software support, service contracts, and vendor escalation to reduce avoidable outages and technical debt. Projects, Vendors, Budget, and Team Development • Assess business needs, evaluate solutions and vendors, develop technical requirements, and lead design, procurement, installation, commissioning, documentation, acceptance testing, and operational handoff for capital and workflow projects. • Develop and manage engineering budgets, forecasts, purchase planning, and expense tracking; present clear options, risks, and lifecycle implications to leadership. • Build strong vendor and corporate-technology relationships, manage escalations, and ensure that work performed by integrators and contractors meets TNND's technical and operational standards. • Coach engineers and technical users, create cross-training and coverage plans, and promote consistent troubleshooting, documentation, safety, and change-control practices. Required Qualifications • Five or more years of progressive experience in television news engineering, broadcast production technology, or an equivalent live-media environment, including demonstrated technical leadership. • Hands-on experience administering or supporting Ross OverDrive automated production control in a live-news environment, including rundown/NRCS integration, device control, show configuration, and troubleshooting under air-critical conditions. • Working expertise with Ross XPression Tessera or Tessera One and XPression-based graphics/display workflows, including multi-display playout, synchronization, signal flow, and operational recovery. • Broad control-room engineering experience with cameras, audio and video systems, production switchers, graphics, routing, multiviewers, intercom, playback/record systems, encoders/decoders, monitoring, and computing infrastructure. • Strong knowledge of broadcast signal flow, baseband and compressed-IP media, shared storage, media workflows, and structured troubleshooting, plus sufficient networking and monitoring knowledge to support TNND workflows and collaborate with Corporate technology teams. • Proficiency supporting Windows, macOS, and Linux platforms and diagnosing hardware, software, network, and workflow failures. • Demonstrated ability to analyze complex operational problems, make sound decisions under pressure, communicate clearly with technical and nontechnical stakeholders, and carry corrective work through completion. • Associate degree or higher in information technology, electronics, computer science, broadcast engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and directly relevant experience. • A collaborative, service-oriented leadership style and a consistent commitment to quality, reliability, documentation, and continuous improvement. Preferred Qualifications • Experience with additional Ross platforms such as XPression, DashBoard/CustomPanels, Carbonite or Acuity production switchers, Ultrix/Ultriscape routing and multiviewing, openGear, or Ross Platform Manager. • Experience with MOS/NRCS integrations, Avid editing and media workflows, media asset management, shared storage, newsroom playout, and multi-platform distribution. • Experience with Amazon Web Services (AWS) and other cloud-native services supporting all-cloud broadcast or media workflows. • Experience partnering with Corporate IT and cybersecurity on access, patching, centralized monitoring, endpoint protection, and secure vendor access for broadcast systems. • Familiarity with applicable FCC requirements, video streaming protocols, SCTE signaling, caption/data workflows, and emerging broadcast standards. • Relevant Avid (including ACSR), SBE, or comparable broadcast-technology certification. Work Expectations • Ability to work a flexible schedule and participate in on-call support, including early mornings, evenings, weekends, holidays, and breaking-news coverage as operational needs require. • Ability to work in control rooms, studios, equipment rooms, offices, and other technical spaces and to safely lift and move computers and equipment generally weighing less than 50 pounds, with reasonable accommodation as applicable. job.title: Solutions Marketing Associate
job.description: The Solutions Marketing Associate helps Sales create more quality client conversations while delivering fast, polished support for everyday opportunities. This role sits closest to the front end of the sales funnel: helping sellers identify the right accounts, do their homework, personalize outreach, and turn established marketing materials into relevant client-facing presentations. For standard and smaller opportunities, typically $100K or less, the Associate uses existing positioning, narratives, templates, research, case studies, and proof points to efficiently build tailored sales materials without recreating strategy from scratch. At the prospecting stage, the Associate gives sellers the account intelligence and lead development support they need to earn more meetings. This role builds the intelligence and inputs behind outreach but does not conduct cold calling, prospecting outreach, or appointment setting. The north star is twofold: help Sales get into more of the right conversations, and help them show up to those conversations prepared. What You’ll Do Prospecting & Meeting Generation Support Identify and research target accounts that fit priority audiences, verticals, solutions, or seller territories. Build and maintain actionable lead and account lists with the context sellers need to prioritize outreach. Research target companies, key contacts, recent business developments, marketing activity, competitive context, and relevant signals that can create a reason to engage. Prepare concise account briefs and outreach inputs that help sellers personalize emails, calls, and meeting requests. Connect prospect needs and business signals to relevant Digital Remedy capabilities, proof points, content, and conversation starters. Partner with Sales on focused prospecting initiatives and campaigns designed to generate qualified meetings. Track which research, prospecting themes, and materials are helping sellers open doors and use those learnings to improve future support. Sales Presentations & Everyday Opportunity Support Support standard and smaller opportunities, typically $100K or less, by tailoring existing presentations and materials to the customer and opportunity. Build polished client-facing decks using established templates, positioning, solution narratives, case studies, research, and proof points. Ensure materials are accurate, on-brand, easy for sellers to present, and aligned with established messaging. Escalate opportunities that require original research, custom strategy, or a new problem-led narrative to the Solutions Marketing Analyst or Manager. Sales Alignment & Enablement Serve as a highly responsive day-to-day partner to Sales, understanding seller priorities, pipeline needs, and recurring friction points. Help sellers navigate available materials, case studies, research, and solution stories so they can self-serve effectively when appropriate. Capture recurring requests and content gaps and share them with the Solutions Marketing Manager and Product & Enablement team. Support broader sales and marketing initiatives that create demand, improve seller preparedness, or accelerate opportunities. What Success Looks Like Sellers have a consistent pipeline of well-researched accounts and stronger reasons to reach out. Prospecting support contributes to more qualified meetings and new sales conversations. Smaller and standard opportunities receive fast, polished, relevant presentation support without unnecessary custom development. Sales spends less time searching for materials and researching accounts and more time engaging customers. The Associate knows when to activate existing materials and when an opportunity should be escalated for deeper strategic support. Strong research instincts and genuine curiosity about companies, industries, buyers, and business challenges. Strong PowerPoint or Google Slides skills and good visual judgment. A proactive, service-oriented mindset paired with the confidence to ask questions and recommend a better path when needed. Familiarity with CRM, prospecting, sales intelligence, and research tools is a plus. Interest in developing toward solutions marketing, insights, strategy, or sales enablement. Together, we amplify our impact, deliver exceptional outcomes, and help our clients succeed in ways that truly matter. Identify Emerging Opportunities: It's about being able to see what others can't, anticipating market shifts, analyzing data and predicting the next big thing. Your insights will position our clients and AMP for long-term success. Strong Communication Skills: You're a natural at building relationships and communicating effectively. Proficiency with digital tools and applications is a must. A Passion for helping Others: You're committed to understanding clients' needs, providing top-notch customer service and making a difference. You're not just selling a product; you're providing a solution. A Competitive Spirit: Do you get a little boost when you achieve a goal (especially if it was a tough one)? We love that for you (and us)! We want someone who's driven to excel but also knows how to celebrate the victories (big and small) with their team. That drive makes you a valuable part of our organization. A Willingness to Grow: Do you thrive in environments where you're always learning something new? Excellent, you'll fit right in! The media world is constantly evolving, and the ability to learn, adapt, and embrace challenges in a fast-paced, digital-first environment is key. We are all for work that is rewarding. The Compensation Package: We offer a base salary, commission structure, and benefits package designed to support your success and well-being. Happy employees don't stage rebellions! ;) We Make a Real Difference (Not Just Talk About It): At AMP, we help local businesses thrive through advertising strategies that create tangible impacts. job.title: Product Manager
job.description: The Product Manager owns the strategy, roadmap, prioritization, and lifecycle management for a portfolio of enterprise applications that includes both custom-developed solutions and third-party SaaS or packaged products. This role partners with business stakeholders, engineering teams, vendors, and support teams to deliver measurable business value, maintain reliable operations, and evolve products in line with user needs and enterprise priorities. Key Responsibilities Product Strategy and Roadmap: Define and maintain product vision, roadmaps, and outcome-based priorities for assigned applications. Balance new capabilities, technical debt, operational stability, compliance, and user experience. Stakeholder Partnership and Discovery: Engage business users and leaders to understand workflows, pain points, opportunities, and success measures. Translate insights into clear, actionable requirements and product decisions. Portfolio and Backlog Management: Own and prioritize the product backlog using business value, risk, effort, dependencies, and strategic alignment. Ensure planned work is sufficiently refined for delivery teams and stakeholders have transparent visibility into priorities. Custom Application Delivery: Work closely with internal development, QA, architecture, and delivery teams throughout discovery, design, development, testing, release, and adoption. Provide timely decisions and clarifications during Agile ceremonies. Third-Party Application Management: Lead the business and product relationship for third-party applications, including vendor coordination, release-impact assessment, roadmap alignment, support escalation, and evaluation of configuration or enhancement opportunities. Requirements and Product Artifacts: Create and maintain product requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, process flows, user experience mock-ups, release communications, and other artifacts needed to align delivery and business teams. Operational Ownership: Partner with production support and vendors to monitor service health, triage issues, communicate business impact, and prioritize corrective work. Help ensure a disciplined transition from delivery to sustainable support. Validation and Adoption: Plan and coordinate user acceptance testing, gather feedback, validate outcomes, and support rollout readiness, training, and adoption activities. Measurement and Continuous Improvement: Define and use product, operational, and adoption metrics to assess performance, identify trends, and drive continuous improvement. Required Experience and Skills Bachelor’s degree in information technology, business, computer science, or a related field; equivalent experience will be considered. Five or more years of product management, product ownership, business analysis, or comparable experience supporting enterprise applications. Experience managing a mix of custom-developed applications, integrations and third-party SaaS or packaged software. Strong ability to turn business needs into well-structured requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and product documentation. Demonstrated ability to prioritize competing demands using data, business value, risk, and operational impact. Working knowledge of Agile delivery practices, including backlog refinement, sprint planning, reviews, and retrospectives. Comfort working with software vendors on product roadmaps, support escalations, releases, and enhancement requests. Strong analytical, communication, facilitation, and stakeholder-management skills; able to lead through influence rather than formal authority. Ability to understand and troubleshoot complex software workflows and communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical audiences. We're looking for someone who understands that weather is one of the biggest drivers of audience engagement across television, streaming, digital, social media, and mobile platforms. You'll be responsible for delivering accurate, compelling forecasts while helping our newsroom own severe weather coverage, producing impactful weather-related stories, and reporting on issues that matter to the communities we serve. Write and update forecasts for our website, mobile apps, and social media. Shoot, write, and edit stories as needed. Explain complex weather in a way that is easy for viewers to understand. Can create compelling digital and social content that extends the life of every forecast. Enjoys experimenting with new technology and finding creative ways to enhance the viewer experience. Experience reporting, shooting, writing, and editing news stories is preferred. Strong knowledge of severe weather forecasting and live television. Experience with weather graphics systems and forecasting technology. Excellent communication, live reporting, and storytelling skills. job.title: Manager, Media Strategy & Business Development
job.description:
The NFL Media Distribution department oversees the strategy, deal execution, and licensing of NFL content across all media platforms. Its core mandate is to grow the business of the National Football League by distributing content in a manner that reaches and engages both new and existing fans, increases revenue for the business, and creates long-term strategic value for the 32 Member Clubs. The group’s work includes market and competitive analysis, new business development, business and rights valuation, deal negotiation, go-to-market process management, and ongoing execution and management of media partnerships.

This person will focus on deepening relationships with current partners, identifying and developing new business opportunities, as well as the formation of strategic partnerships and alliances. This role requires a strong self-starter who can combine a solid understanding and interest of the media space with a comprehensive foundation in business analysis. This role works closely with many departments across the NFL’s New York, New Jersey and Los Angeles offices including Broadcasting, Sponsorship, DTC Strategy, Affiliate, Media Sales, Legal, Finance, Marketing and NFL Digital Media Product & Engineering Teams.

Responsibilities include leading regular communication with external and internal business partners (day-to-day project and product management), producing financial models and presentations for executives and external partners, working closely with Legal to develop new legal contracts, and thoughtfully managing internal stakeholders and processes (seeking internal feedback, escalating issues, proposing recommendations, etc.).

Responsibilities

  • Take a meaningful role in all aspects of NFL media partnerships, from working on large-scale active partnerships to proactively identifying potential new business partners
  • Assess and analyze critical media and sports trends
  • Oversee day-to-day activity with current partners to ensure contractual obligations are met and all parties and relationships are mutually successful
  • Conduct financial analyses and proposals for new business opportunities
  • Collaborate with senior executives and relevant internal stakeholders to develop new contracts and deals
  • Communicate market and deal updates to senior executives and team ownership
  • Create and participate in strategic presentations to senior executives inside and outside the organization
  • Track consumption trends across media partnerships
  • Advance league-wide initiatives in collaboration with teams across the organization
  • Contribute to positive group culture to foster high performance, efficient processes and professional development

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree
  • Minimum 5+ years of experience, ideally in media, consulting or financial services

Other Key Attributes / Characteristics

  • Strong attention to detail, especially when multi-tasking across various projects in a fast-paced environment; expected to execute tasks with minimal error and with high level of efficiency
  • Deep interest and enthusiasm in media, technology and sports industries with ability to apply market trends to inform strategic decisions
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to clearly articulate details to senior management
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to conduct financial and business/market analyses and distill key insights for stakeholders
  • Effective partner facing communication and presence with large and small partners
  • A team player who is able to establish credibility quickly in order to effectively interface at all levels in a complex organization
  • Strong, confident personal style that can persuade and motivate others to accomplish corporate goals while holding team members accountable to a high standard of performance
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills, including the ability to efficiently produce written materials and analysis in Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint
  • Unwavering commitment to honest and ethical business interactions
  • Exceptional work ethic and positive attitude

Terms / Expected Hours of Work

  • NFL employees are required to work 40 hours per week.
  • Travel occasionally

Salary / Pay Range

This job posting contains a pay range, which represents the range of salaries or hourly rates that the NFL believes, in good faith, at the time of this posting that it might be willing to pay for the posted job in the location(s) specified. The NFL expects to hire for this position near the middle of the range. Only in truly rare and exceptional circumstances, where an external candidate has experience, credentials or expertise that far exceed those required or expected for the position, would the NFL consider paying a salary or rate near the higher end of the range.

Salary
$90,000—$125,000 USD

Benefits Information
To learn more about our comprehensive benefits offerings, please visit: NFL BENEFITS

At the NFL, in-person work at our offices is a top priority because it allows us to collaborate more effectively, build stronger connections, and maintain the culture that drives our success. This role requires onsite presence at an NFL office or stadium location, and remote and/or hybrid working options are not offered.

NO RELOCATION ASSISTANCE WILL BE PROVIDED.

The NFL is committed to building an inclusive work environment that reflects our incredible fan base. We provide an environment of mutual respect where equal employment opportunities are available to all employees and applicants without regard to status as protected by applicable federal, state, and local laws.

NFL Core Values:

  • Respect: Everyone matters. We celebrate diverse opinions, honor hard work, and value every contribution.
  • Integrity: We do what's right, even when it's tough. We hold ourselves accountable and always follow through.
  • Team Responsibility: We support each other and our communities. No one is bigger than the game, and every action impacts others.
  • Resiliency: We set high standards, overcome adversity, and adapt to challenges, always striving for excellence.

  • Build Talent: We develop and nurture potential, empowering individuals to grow and succeed.

  • Inspire: We motivate others through vision, energy, and a commitment to excellence.

  • Know the Business: We stay informed, understand our industry, and make decisions that strengthen our position.
  • Think Big: We challenge the status quo, envision bold possibilities, and strive for transformative impact

WHO YOU ARE:

  • Embody an enthusiastic, proactive can-do attitude
  • Embrace grit, free from ego or entitlement
  • Excel as a relationship builder, with the ability to influence
  • Eager learner, driven by passion rather than just ambition

job.description: About ASCAP The American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers (ASCAP) is a membership association of more than one million songwriters, composers and music publishers, and represents some of the world’s most talented music creators. Founded and governed by songwriters, composers and publishers, it is the only performing rights organization in the U.S. that operates on a not-for-profit basis. ASCAP licenses a repertory of over 20 million musical works to hundreds of thousands of businesses that use music, including streaming services, cable television, radio and satellite radio and brick and mortar businesses such as retail stores, hotels, clubs, restaurants and bars. ASCAP collects the licensing fees; identifies, matches and processes trillions of performances every year; and returns nearly 90 cents of every dollar back to its members as royalties. The ASCAP blanket license offers an efficient solution for businesses to legally perform ASCAP music while respecting the right of songwriters and composers to be paid fairly. ASCAP puts music creators first, advocating for their rights and the value of music on Capitol Hill, driving innovation that moves the industry forward, building community and providing the resources and support that creators need to succeed in their careers. CPCD Analysts weigh performances based on their knowledge of the musical genre, instrumentation, and style before entering new title records into the database. Concert Program Analysts are also responsible for maintaining and updating work records with any newly received information. As an audience editor, you will report to Wirecutter's deputy director of newsletters and programming, and collaborate closely with colleagues across newsletters and programming, audience at large, Wirecutter's newsroom, as well as our commerce, marketing, product, and analytics teams.

You will drive the editorial voice of Store-related messaging, build and maintain a unified promo calendar, and design tests and experiments to deepen engagement while valuing Wirecutter's standards for independence and trust.

  • Contribute to overall Wirecutter newsletters and programming responsibilities — especially during major moments where it connects to the Store (i.e. gifting season; deal events).

  • Continuously test and optimize messaging (subject lines, CTAs, timing, sequencing) to improve engagement while staying rooted in our standards and reporting.

  • Excellent editorial judgment, line-editing skills, and a strong sense of how to translate rigorous reporting into clear, compelling, and trustworthy copy.

job.title: China Correspondent
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.

The New York Times is looking for an experienced journalist to cover China.

China’s transformation to geopolitical and economic colossus over the past several decades has bolstered its confidence at home and its influence abroad. Beijing has leveraged its might, both commercially and militarily, to redraw the terms of trade, security and diplomacy. Under Xi Jinping’s leadership, China has sought to offer a model of governance that challenges the liberal democratic order and the dominance of the United States.

China is one of the biggest stories we cover, and one of the most challenging. It’s also one of the most exciting, a constantly changing and diverse country with few parallels on the planet. It touches nearly every major issue. Geopolitics. Demographics. Inequality. Climate Change. Trade. Technology.

The role requires a strong writer with the ability to juggle breaking news, smart analysis and ambitious enterprise. We want someone eager to react quickly to news as necessary, but who is also able to write thoughtfully and deeply about important issues and events. We are looking for an entrepreneurial correspondent who can embrace the multitudes, to cover the news and the nuance.

This position will be based in Beijing, China, or elsewhere in Asia.

Main responsibilities:

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our values of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • Deliver timely coverage of major breaking news events about China and its influence in the region, providing clarity, accuracy, and sharp analytical context for a global audience.
  • Conceive, pitch, and execute ambitious enterprise stories and deeply reported features that reveal the nuances of political, societal and demographic shifts, economic inequality, and cultural trends.
  • Track and analyze China’s expanding global footprint, reporting on how Beijing leverages its commercial, technological, and military might to reshape international trade, climate policy, and global diplomacy.
  • Cultivate and maintain a diverse and robust network of sources— including policymakers, businesspeople, scholars, commentators and ordinary citizens—while navigating a highly restrictive and complex reporting environment with resilience and integrity.
  • Collaborate across formats, partnering closely with Photo, Video, Audio and Graphics teams to produce visually rich, immersive journalism that elevates our storytelling.
  • Work collegially with the broader China bureau and regional editors in Asia, as well as the broader international desk.

Qualifications:

  • Deep international reporting experience, preferably for a global news organization.
  • Experience working in China and/or fluency in Mandarin.
  • A keen eye for news and other great stories, borne of experience reporting and writing.
  • Eagerness to collaborate with colleagues across Photo, Video, Audio and other departments to bring stories to life in a variety of formats.
  • A constant drive to develop and maintain new sources, and a commitment to fairness and independence in reporting and presentation.
  • Commitment to The New York Times’s standards and mission.

In order to be considered for this role, please submit your resume, a PDF/link of your top 5-7 clips, and a coverage memo laying out the themes and some specific stories you would want to take on.

job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. The International Desk is seeking a Conflict Operations Editor. This is a dedicated newsroom role for a veteran journalist who has demonstrated sharp judgment and leadership working in security-sensitive assignments. You will help guide our most ambitious and complicated newsgathering efforts, in close partnership with our security team.

You will work closely with the International Editor and the desk’s top leaders to navigate the challenges of reporting in conflict zones and other difficult environments and ensure that the safety and security of our staff is a top priority. You will direct correspondents in the field, serve as a partner to their editors and coordinate with our security advisers and newsroom leadership. You will assess risk and make tough calls while building systems to support our journalists around the world in an era of prolonged and changing war.

This is an in-office position preferably based in London, and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per departmental guidance. You will also be expected to deploy internationally as news events dictate.

Responsibilities:

  • Build and guide newsgathering operations: The primary goal of this position is to inform and ensure we’re making the right calls on assignments in security-sensitive locations. With guidance and close partnership from our security experts, you will collaborate with senior editors to make the tough decisions on editorial necessity and safety to ensure the safety of our teams in the field.
  • Leadership Briefings: Provide daily situation and staffing updates for newsroom editors and leadership. Investigate and analyze security incidents and issues to find vulnerabilities and enact corrective measures as needed so we are continuously improving our systems.
  • Establishing Conflict Bureaus: Deploy quickly to rapidly create or scale wartime bureaus. Work with security and the bureau chief to secure and vet critical local infrastructure and ensure our on-the-ground presence and operation supports safety and exceptional journalism.
  • Business continuity: Lead disaster recovery, evacuation planning and crisis management in partnership with our business continuity team.
  • Operational Security : Work in close partnership with the security operation to ensure teams have the specific gear and training required for their assignments, and that we’re following proper protocols to enable our journalists to stay safe while doing their jobs.
  • Freelancer & Evacuee Support: In collaboration with Legal and Global Operations, coordinate support for our freelancers in conflict zones, and for Times journalists who have had to relocate or evacuate due to conflicts.
  • Digital Security: Work with our information security team to ensure that journalists in sensitive environments have their data, devices and sources properly protected.
  • Journalistic values: Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

This role reports to the International Editor, based in New York.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Experience working with journalists in conflict zones
  • Experience in a role requiring high-level operational skills and crisis management.
  • Excellent news judgment and understanding of journalistic imperatives.
  • Strong communication skills, able to brief and advise leadership with clarity
  • Strong collaboration skills, with experience working across a broad range of stakeholders and partners.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Extensive experience in journalism, including significant time as a correspondent or editor in security-sensitive places.
  • Demonstrated experience managing local teams (fixers, drivers, interpreters) in volatile or hostile environments.
  • Demonstrated organizational and process-management skills
  • Willingness to travel internationally, including to security-sensitive locations on short notice.

job.title: Correspondent, The Economics of a Warming World
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.

Climate change is reshaping insurance markets, agriculture, supply chains, labor productivity, real estate, facility planning and the flow of capital and trade globally. It is a central force reordering how industries make decisions and compelling societies to make difficult choices about how to spend scarce resources. It is pulsing through economies, but often goes unrecognized.

We’re creating a new beat to fix that.

This correspondent will reveal the economic implications of a warming planet. It’s one of the most significant coverage areas in the world today, touching on energy and trade, shifting global economic alliances and the complex calculations being made by societies that may determine prosperity or poverty for generations.

The mandate spans everything from why insurers are pulling out of entire states, to how ports are redesigning for rising seas, to how central banks are beginning to price climate risk into monetary policy and ways that a warming world is forcing governments to spend more.

This correspondent will also have the investigative skills to reveal which entities are profiting from a changing climate and how they use power and money to their advantage, influencing markets and government policies.

This is a rare opportunity to define a beat from scratch.

This is an in-office position and includes regular attendance in a NYT office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Report ahead of the curve and break news — Curiosity that leads you to identify which industries, regions, or asset classes are about to face a climate reckoning before it becomes obvious to the public or even to the industries themselves. We want stories nobody else has found
  • Write standout features that use narratives and data to make abstract risk tangible: the Iowa farmer recalibrating for a new growing season, the Miami condo board fighting over special assessments, the highway engineer redesigning for freeze-thaw cycles that no longer freeze.
  • Illuminate how climate risk is moving through the economy: insurance repricing, credit downgrades, corporate disclosures, agricultural futures, real estate valuations and municipal bond markets and write about it in an engaging, accessible way
  • Translate science into economic consequences — fluently connecting climate models, weather data, and physical risk research to markets, prices, and policy with graceful language that leads readers to say ”Now I understand!”
  • Build a network of sources across insurance, agriculture, utilities, construction, banking, and academia
  • Collaborate with Business, Real Estate, National, Weather and other desks to produce ambitious work
  • Think visually, and work in different formats, including video and data visualization
  • Explain complexity clearly for readers who may know nothing about, for example, reinsurance markets
  • Tell the big picture, be able to stand back, connect events and see the larger narrative in the United States and abroad
  • Dig, be able to dive below the surface, follow the money and illuminate hidden deals and decisions

Basic Qualifications

  • 5+ years of reporting experience, ideally spanning business/economics journalism with some exposure to science, policy, or climate reporting
  • Fluency in economics and markets — you should be as comfortable reading a Fed statement as a peer-reviewed climate study
  • A track record of enterprise reporting and investigative work
  • A fluid, clear and vivid writing style; the ability to not just report but to tell a story. Good writing is a must.
  • Demonstrated range — the ability to turn a daily news story and a 4,000-word feature with equal skill
  • Experience with public records requests, financial disclosures, or regulatory filings as reporting tools
  • Comfort with data: the ability to interrogate a dataset and recognize the story in the numbers
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Preferred Skills

  • Prior beat experience in insurance, agriculture, real estate, infrastructure, or energy markets
  • Familiarity with climate science literature and modeling (IPCC reports, NOAA/NASA data, catastrophe modeling)
  • A network of sources in insurance, banking, agribusiness, or public works

Why This Role

You'll be building something new: a beat that springs from one of the biggest stories of our time — a changing climate — with the resources, editing, and platform of The New York Times behind you. Your reporting will help readers, policymakers, and business leaders understand risks and opportunities most of the world hasn't yet digested.

*To be considered for this role, please submit your resume and cover letter, including links to 5-7 clips that demonstrate your range.

The Analytics Data Products team builds the foundational data products and pipelines that make that possible, and we're looking for a Data Engineer to help us build them. You'll own and enhance the data pipelines and core, reusable data products that partner teams across the company depend on to unlock analytics for their most important questions. You'll work hands-on across our hybrid cloud architecture (AWS and GCP) and contribute to the platform that delivers trusted data products company-wide spanning multiple business domains. You'll join a collaborative team that invests in your growth. Reporting to the Senior Engineering Manager of Analytics Data Products, you'll take ownership of pipelines and products, learn from experienced engineers, and grow your impact across the company.

This is a hybrid role in our New York City headquarters.

  • Design, model, and implement complex data pipelines for the cleansed and curated data layers in the medallion architecture, taking full ownership of the data product's structure, partitioning, documentation, and performance characteristics.

  • Develop advanced data transformations using dbt (data build tool) for relational data modeling and PySpark for complex data processing within the Lakehouse, ensuring outputs meet strict SLAs and quality standards.

  • Collaborate with Data Analysts and other consumers to define requirements and translate them into scalable data models suitable for analytic use cases.

  • Contribute to the implementation of metadata management, data lineage, and role-based access control (RBAC) programs across the Lakehouse environment.

  • Hands-on experience with a Cloud Data Warehouse (BigQuery, Snowflake, DataBricks)

    • Manage budget and expenses for the Office of the GM.

    • Support multiple leaders on an individual level, primarily by:

      • Managing and prioritizing complex calendars, serving as a thoughtful gatekeeper of time and requests to ensure leaders focus on the highest-impact work.

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

The New York Times is looking for a Director, HR Business Partner for the Global Advertising group to support and partner with leaders, managers and employees across the Advertising, Marketing, Communications, Licensing, and Strategic Partnerships functions. You will manage a team of two, while also supporting employees directly. You will report to the SVP, Global HR Business Partners.

The Director, HRBP plays a critical role in driving a people strategy aligned with enterprise goals. You will be the primary HR partner to support our Chief Advertising Officer and SVP, Partnerships, managers, and employees of the assigned client groups - including guidance, management of the performance enablement cycle, and oversight of process/HR administration.

This role is based at The New York Times headquarters in New York, NY, and is eligible for a hybrid working schedule.

Responsibilities:

  • Be an advisor, partner and coach to senior leaders, managers, and individual contributors across our Advertising group.
  • Lead and develop a team of two HR Business Partners to manage multiple HR issues and support the business.
  • Provide daily support to senior-level department leaders, managers, and employees, providing coaching, management of employee lifecycles and performance management, and oversight of process/HR administration.
  • Lead planning, communication support and implementation of company and department-level people initiatives, developing programs and solutions to meet department needs.
  • Partner with Centers of Excellence (COEs) to deliver impactful people initiatives to client groups. Provide COEs with clear, relevant feedback on how to refine and enhance people initiatives over time.
  • Partner with leadership to monitor how business plans and industry trends may affect talent needs, HR priorities, and the way your client groups are organized or operate.
  • Partner with business leaders on setting priorities and monitoring progress to create an inclusive workplace for all employees.
  • Develop and interpret relevant people metrics to identify trends and provide insights that shape HR strategy and talent recommendations, and lead cross-functional initiatives.
  • Collaborate with Employee Relations, Talent Management, and Legal teams to investigate and resolve employee relations issues, ensure regulatory compliance, and identify development needs for employees.
  • Handle daily operational tasks, such as answering requests and inquiries from employees and assisting with HRIS transactions.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of increasing HR Business Partner experience and responsibility with experience managing a range of HR disciplines, including employee relations, employment law, labor relations, talent management and development, compensation, and inclusion within Advertising or adjacent creative teams.
  • 5+ years of experience leading people, with a focus on developing a motivated, engaged, and inclusive team.
  • Experience working with an HRIS, e.g. Workday, SuccessFactors.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent in HR, business, psychology or a relevant field.
  • SPHR or equivalent professional accreditation.
  • Experience working in a matrixed global public company. Advertising, Media or similar industry.

job.description:
