job.title: Senior Video Editor, Wild Card
job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide.

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Application Deadline: Please submit your application by 11:59 pm EST September 14th, 2026

About the Position

Wild Card with Rachel Martin is an interview show that serves as an antidote to the cynicism and chaos of modern life. Rachel’s soulful conversations with some of the most influential and thoughtful minds of our generation reminds people of the things that matter most.

In 2025, Wild Card launched as NPR’s first-ever video podcast. Since then, Rachel’s interviews with everyone from Oprah to Michelle Obama have reached millions of views on YouTube and clips from the show regularly go viral on Instagram. NPR is looking for an experienced video editor to help Wild Card further develop its video presence and reach new audiences.

We’re looking for a creative and organized video editor with experience booking, producing and editing longform interviews. You’ll produce, edit, and publish long- and short-form video for Wild Card. You have a strong understanding of how distribution and virality works on platforms like Spotify, YouTube and Instagram. You will support showrunners, podcast hosts, and work closely with NPR’s Visuals team. You will innovate new formats and design approaches to help Wild Card reach bigger audiences.

This is a union-represented role covered under the terms of a collective bargaining agreement with SAG-AFTRA.

This is an NPR editorial role covered under the terms of the NPR Ethics Handbook. All editorial staff are bound by this guidance. Editorial staff are defined as staff members who play a role in shaping the journalistic or creative direction of NPR's content, including events.

Responsibilities

  • Collaborate with producers and editors on Wild Card to conceive, generate, edit and publish video podcast episodes and short-form vertical video.
  • Collaborate with Wild Card editors on managing Instagram, YouTube and other visual platforms.
  • Manage production schedule for multiple video editors working on weekly Wild Card video deliverables.
  • Produce, edit and publish audio deliverables for radio and other audio-only platforms
  • Direct remote and in-person Wild Card tapings
  • Pitch and book guests who have the right mix of thoughtfulness, vulnerability and humor to match Wild Card’s tone.
  • Take responsibility for video tasks, including multiple layers of coordination, logistics, creativity and sensitivity in the storytelling.
  • Work with the Wild Card and visuals teams to figure out new formats for Wild Card content that will help reach new audiences.
  • Help refine Wild Card’s presentation on major video platforms, including thumbnails, titles, landing pages, etc.
  • Excel at directing and executing visual storytelling forms such as cinematography, photography and lighting, as well as be proficient at executing motion graphics, where applicable.
  • Clearly communicate the vision, project goals, narrative scope and timeline for each production.
  • Function as a key decision maker on the shape and look of regular content and important projects.
  • Maintain NPR editorial and ethical guidelines in all production.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years video production experience, preferably with a major network or newsroom, studio or creative agency.
  • Mastery of Riverside, Descript, Premiere, and other programs related to video, photo and design, including Canva.
  • Experience producing video interviews
  • Experience with social media engagement is a plus.
  • Demonstrated commitment to increasing audience diversity.
  • Be well-versed in copyright and ethical journalism practices.
  • Excellent communication and writing skills.
  • Strong editing skills.
  • Must be able to lift video equipment weighing up to 30 pounds.

The Senior Director, Digital Development at Columbia Records builds the viral foundation for projects before they scale. Where the wider Viral Marketing team drives influencer campaigns at volume around established artists and priority singles, this role sits at the front end: developing artists, first singles, early-stage projects, and catalog titles showing early signals of movement.

The work is diagnostic, strategic, and hands-on. Read the audience quickly, map the niches that matter, find and test the content that actually works inside them, and run point on the seeding that puts it in front of the right communities. Once a project has traction and a proven approach, it transitions to a Viral Marketing lead to scale further. The role sits within the Viral Marketing team at Columbia Records and works alongside Marketing, Audience and Social teams from project kickoff.

What you'll do:

  • Own the viral strategy for developing artists and early-stage projects, from pre-release through the first signs of traction, before campaigns move into scaled execution.
  • Build a fast, accurate read on each project’s audience: who they are, where they sit online, what they already engage with, and what the artist’s credible entry point is.
  • Map and pressure-test the niches and creator communities around a project (subcultures, formats, sounds, references) and identify where the artist has real cultural permission to land.
  • Identify and test content angles inside those niches at low cost and high frequency. Prove what works before budget scales.
  • Run point on seeding strategy and execution for early-stage projects: set the seeding plan, choose the communities and accounts, brief the content, and place it. This is hands-on work, not oversight.
  • Build and maintain the seeding infrastructure the front end of a campaign depends on: page networks, community accounts, creator relationships, and the process for moving content through them quickly.
  • Establish the creative foundation each campaign scales from: the hook, the format, the angle, the seeding logic, documented clearly enough for the wider Viral team to run with it.
  • Work closely with the Catalog and Legacy divisions to surface titles showing early signals of growth, and build viral strategies around them fast enough to catch the moment.
  • Monitor catalog and recent releases for emergent movement (UGC velocity, sound usage, search and DSP behavior, playlist and platform signals) and flag opportunities proactively rather than reactively.
  • Partner with Marketing, Audience and Social from kickoff so viral strategy is built into the campaign, not bolted on afterward.
  • Build early relationships with creators and micro-communities relevant to developing projects, where fit matters more than reach.
  • Transition proven projects to the Viral Marketing leads with a clear strategy, evidence of what works, and the seeding and community groundwork in place.
  • Report findings, tests, and results to senior staff, translating early signal into recommendations the wider team can act on.

Who you are:

  • 7+ years professional experience in influencer, social, or digital marketing, with significant time spent on early-stage artists, emerging brands, or projects built without an existing audience.
  • Hands-on seeding experience: has personally built and run seeding operations, not only directed them. Familiar with page networks, community accounts, and the mechanics of placing content at speed.
  • Track record of setting strategy that other teams execute, and of influencing senior stakeholders across departments without direct authority over them.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify and build inside niche online communities, not only mainstream creator channels.
  • Strong instinct for internet culture paired with the research discipline to back it up. Fluent across TikTok, Instagram, YouTube Shorts, and the adjacent platforms where subcultures form.
  • Experience testing content and reading results quickly. Comfortable being wrong fast and adjusting.
  • Working knowledge of streaming and consumption data, DSP behavior, and third-party trend tools.
  • Genuine knowledge of music history and catalog, and real interest in why older records find new audiences.
  • In-depth knowledge of music culture, trends, and creator communities.
  • Clear written communication. This role produces the strategy that others scale.
  • Self-directed and comfortable with ambiguity, able to move on projects that do not yet have structure around them.
  • Experience mentoring or developing junior team members, with the judgment to build process where it is needed and leave it out where it is not.
  • Experience with AI tools to accelerate research and streamline workflow where appropriate.

job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.

Job Description

The New York Times' Advertising team is looking for an Ads Solutions and Campaign Management Intern to join the team. As an Ads Solutions and Campaign Management intern, you will support the post-sale creative production, trafficking, delivery and reporting of digital campaigns across The New York Times portfolio. You will work closely with Campaign Managers and Producers to ensure that advertiser creatives align with client expectations and that campaigns are set up accurately, deliver on schedule and meet our quality standards.


About The Role

This internship is an opportunity to gain hands-on experience and training in digital creative production and ad operations within a global, premium publisher environment. This is a hybrid role based in our Paris headquarters, reporting to the Director, Ad Solutions & Operations. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week. The position will start from September for a duration of 6 months, based in Paris. Candidates must have the right to work in France for the full duration of the internship.

  • This internship is intended for students or recent graduates who meet the legal requirements for an internship (stage) in France with a mandatory “Convention de stage”.
  • To apply, please submit:
    • Your CV
    • A short cover letter explaining your interest in digital advertising and this specific role

Responsibilities:

  • Support Ad Solutions in the creative production process:
    • Helping compile specs and example executions for clients based on signed media plans
    • Reviewing assets for technical specification compliancy
    • Customising units according to client guidelines using CSS3
    • Testing ads across browsers, screen sizes and devices
  • Support Campaign Managers with the end-to-end setup of digital campaigns, including:
    • Collecting and validating creative assets and tracking tags
    • Trafficking campaigns in GAM, AdSwizz and LiveIntent
  • Assist in monitoring live campaigns:
    • Reviewing pacing and delivery reports
    • Flagging under-delivery or issues to the Campaign Manager in a timely manner
    • Supporting optimisations based on performance and client objectives
  • Contribute to campaign reporting:
    • Pulling performance data from ad servers and other platforms
    • Assisting in the preparation of client-facing reports and post-campaign summaries
  • Support day-to-day operations:
    • Collaborating with Sales, Planning and other internal stakeholders on campaign-related tasks
    • Maintaining internal dashboards and trackers as required
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Interest in digital advertising
  • Experience working with numbers and spreadsheets (e.g. basic formulas, filtering and pivot tables in Excel/Google Sheets)
  • Experience with a detailed and structured working style
  • Experience prioritizing competing programs, responsibilities, and projects
  • Professional proficiency in English

  • Basic understanding of digital advertising concepts (impressions, clicks, CTR, viewability, targeting, etc.)
  • Familiarity with HTML5, CSS3 and JS.

job.title: Newsroom Strategy Manager
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.

The New York Times Newsroom Strategy team is looking for a Strategy Manager with journalism, strategy and data experience to help shape and advance the newsroom’s biggest goals.

This is an important and exciting moment to work in strategy at The Times. Our journalism has never been stronger or more relevant, and our newsroom continues to expand with an ever-wider array of beats, formats and expertise. At the same time, a rapidly changing media ecosystem presents significant opportunities as well as challenges, from changing audience habits to video and A.I.

The Newsroom Strategy team works with Times leaders to help the newsroom chart and implement our strategy. From coverage to audience to operations, we help identify long-term opportunities, set priorities and accomplish them. The team has helped to shape our major recent video investment; expanded our journalism with new coverage initiatives and investments in areas like Live, Well and local; and partnered with teams like Audience and Security to strengthen critical parts of our journalism operation.

As a Manager on the team, you will lead projects, undertake analysis and recommend paths forward to ensure we are maximizing our impact. You’ll take a reporter’s eye to The Times and our priorities — spotting and investigating opportunities and challenges — and develop plans to address them. We will look to you for insightful research, data analysis and problem solving; effective partnership with stakeholders; and an enterprising and collaborative spirit. You’ll work closely with colleagues across the organization – journalists, audience and data, corporate strategy, finance, product, HR and others.

In all your work, you’ll be rooted in our journalistic mission and the value of independence, and ensure that we are considering a wide range of perspectives from inside and outside The Times.

This role reports to the deputy editor for Newsroom Strategy and is based in New York, with regular attendance in the office at least four days each week.

Responsibilities:

  • Deliver high-quality analyses and recommendations for strategy projects:
    • Break down complex problems and opportunities
    • Conduct research and interviews
    • Analyze quantitative and qualitative info to uncover insights
    • Ideal: Analyze data using SQL and transform big data into visualizations
    • Develop practical solutions and plans to implement them
  • Build advisory relationships and trusting partnerships
  • Convey complex ideas in a clear and compelling way – in writing and in person
  • Operate in an enterprising and efficient manner with moderate oversight
  • Demonstrate strong journalistic and ethical judgment, and work in accordance with our journalistic values and standards

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of relevant work experience
  • Experience in a journalism or other relevant media role
  • Experience producing strategic research and analyses, including data and financial models
  • Experience communicating recommendations to senior leaders in writing (e.g., memos, slide presentations) and verbally
  • Experience breaking down complex problems into pieces that can be solved with data, analysis, and clear assumptions
  • Passion for journalism and commitment to The Times’ mission and values

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience working in a newsroom
  • Deep interest in and understanding of trends and challenges facing journalism and the media industry, and The Times in particular
  • Sound journalistic judgment, with an eye for innovative coverage opportunities
  • Clear and concise communication style
  • Fluency in AI tools and technology
  • Technical data experience, including proficiency with SQL, comfort with version control (Github, code review), experience with dashboarding tools (Mode, Tableau, etc.) and familiarity with BigQuery or other big data environments

job.title: Program Lead, Suno Emerging Creator Program (Contract)
job.description: About Suno We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world. Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible. Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA). About the Program Suno's mission is amplifying creativity for people everywhere. Having built strong traction with emerging musicians and producers, our next opportunity is the content creator economy. Suno’s new Emerging Creator Program launches that effort: developing the next generation of creators while establishing Suno as a company that accelerates creative careers. The program is a selective, cohort-based 12-week experience for a cohort of nano and micro creators building careers around content. Members get access to exclusive programming including Suno workshops and keynotes from breakout creators, plus creative contests, content spotlights, IRL events, and a network of fellow creators. At the end of the program, we aim to sign a few participants for ongoing deals with Suno, maintain an active community of creators, and scale the initiative beyond the pilot phase. The Role You'll be the operational engine of the program: building it from the ground up alongside the Suno team through August and September, then running it end-to-end through December. You'll own the calendar, the cohort experience, the speakers, the events, and all of the details in between. In this role you’ll have the opportunity to work closely with Growth and Influencer marketing, Music partnerships and Creative to turn this from strategy and vision into reality. What You'll Do Build Translate the program outline into a week-by-week curriculum: session formats, Suno skills/tools coverage, contest design for off weeks Build and manage the guest speaker pipeline: identify, pitch, confirm, and prep breakout-creator speakers and mentors Stand up program infrastructure: community channel (Slack/Discord), calendar, meeting/tech setup, application intake and tracking Support outreach and sourcing: manage the handpicked invite list, Spark referrals, and application pipeline; run logistics for the selection process (Sept 7–18) Determine application approach, launch messaging, and launch-creator partnership Source and negotiate member perks with partner tools and brands Coordinate internal reviews (including legal review of contest mechanics, creator payments, event liability, and minors) Run Own the biweekly programming cadence end-to-end: scheduling, speaker coordination, session production, follow-ups Run monthly creative contests: briefs, submission tracking, judging logistics, prize fulfillment Design and manage the creator spotlight approach Produce IRL moments if applicable Be the day-to-day face of the program for members: onboarding, questions, nudges, community management, keeping energy high Track program health: attendance, participation, contest engagement, member sentiment; flag at-risk members early Assess Produce the graduation moment: credentialing, culmination for participants Transition the cohort into the alumni network Deliver a program retro: what worked, what didn't, and a recommended blueprint for cohort 2 Who You Are You've operated programs like this before: 3+ years running cohort-based programs, creator/community programs, accelerators, fellowships, or high-touch event series, ideally you’ve built one from scratch. You know the creator economy: You understand how nano/micro creators think about growth, money, brands, and community and you can talk to them credibly. Bonus: you've worked with creator programs, MCNs, talent management, or platform partnerships You're an ops machine: Calendars, run-of-shows, trackers, follow-ups. You're the person who notices the Zoom link is wrong before anyone joins You’re hospitality-minded and a strong experience designer: Members should feel the program is run by someone who gets them. You create belonging, and intuitively know what people need and how to serve them. You work autonomously: You are excited by ambiguity and the ability to create structure from guardrails. You’re communicative, independent and reliable. Bonus: experience producing IRL events; familiarity with Suno or AI creative tools; existing relationships with breakout creators or creator communities What Success Looks Like Program launches on time at full capacity 12 weeks of programming run smoothly with strong attendance and completion Members describe the program as career-changing, say so publicly A documented playbook that makes cohort 2 easier, bigger, or better Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.
